codeReviewConclusions: Task execution is a bounded structured DAG; Mermaid is its deterministic canonical projection, never a second writable execution source.
The backend checks DAG/required gates and official Mermaid parsing/projection before independent fresh read-only Agent and batched Jev semantics run in parallel.
Goal, workflow-design and Mermaid results stay separate; malformed structure, missing evidence or unresolved semantic objections cannot be replaced by high Jev probabilities.
Planning review is a control-plane operation and cannot satisfy post-implementation verification/review/math gates.
Current request, contract, workflow, policy and parser/generator bindings are compared before publishing review and before enforced execution/acceptance.
Missing Jev permits only explicitly labelled degradation when the policy allows it; semantic objections or incomplete answers remain review_required.
The client now exposes three dimensions and evidence/error locations while separating Agent/Jev opinions from syntax/projection checks; absent results remain not reviewed.
The settings editor preserves bounded opaque route policy in regular and upgrade chains, so unrelated settings saves do not erase quota-domain isolation.

remainingPlanScopeAndLimits: P4 real paired task/model usage and quality experiments are not complete; the local benchmark report explicitly leaves the claimed 28% token saving unknown.
End-to-end live generation/Jev account behavior, strict billing completeness and user-workload quality require actual provider instrumentation and permitted service calls.
API/native capabilities must remain separately reported; API test success does not imply native P2P tool binding or hard isolation.
Mermaid depicts a single-round execution DAG; repair control is bounded in runtime rounds and diagnostics, not a general graph scheduler.
Current planning-record reuse is not evidence that all Jev entry points have a universal shared result cache or that expert live contexts have an implemented eviction/watermark policy.
Persistence reconstructs audited state and fresh expert context where supported; it does not promise resume of an old live thread or distributed multi-owner NFS writes.
Root must run and bind final typecheck, complete unit/integration suites and source hashes after the remaining parallel regressions; this report is not an unconditional release certificate.
